intent.subject: Corporal Mahmoud (C-04), the radio operator, in profile with taped wire-rimmed glasses.
intent.action: He lifts his gaze from the decoded note and whispers the warning, his lips slightly parted.
intent.setting: Tina Plain marsh at night (LOC-0003), with a red-filtered flashlight illuminating the paper and catching on his glasses while the surrounding frame falls into deep shadow.

research.claim: The company is shown beginning its march through the Tina Plain/marsh after the early helicopter drop.
research.note: Follows production decision D-1 to use the Egyptian account of the early Tina Plain drop and long march; the landing location and march distance remain disputed and require the episode end-card source note.

research.claim: The precise setting of this first-march moment as full night is not explicitly established in the ledger.
research.note: H-05 and H-08 support the drop and march, but do not establish this beat's exact time of night.

research.claim: Composite Corporal Mahmoud sends/receives and decodes the coded radio traffic, warns Shalabi that the signal was intercepted, worries about losing contact with command, and switches off the set.
research.note: Mahmoud is a composite character. His actions dramatize the sourced intercepted-signal and radio-silence event without assigning it to a documented real individual.

research.claim: Captain Hamdi Shalabi orders radio silence after the intercepted-signal warning.
research.note: The coded warning and Shalabi's radio-silence order are stated by the primary Egyptian account; the marked dialogue is a permitted dramatized paraphrase.

research.claim: Shalabi taps the switched-off radio and draws a finger across his lips to communicate the sourced radio-silence order; the file passes the silent signal back man to man.
research.note: Permitted staging under P-01: the gestures visually show the sourced radio-silence order and add no new event or outcome.

research.claim: Composite Sergeant Sayed hears the silence order and asks whether the enemy is waiting for them.
research.note: Sayed is a composite character; the question is fictional character dialogue and does not credit him with a documented act.

research.claim: Shalabi uses his compass, changes the file's bearing, and directs the company toward an unexpected approach after the interception warning.
research.note: The route-change dialogue is an approved paraphrase of the source treatment that the enemy did not expect anyone to come from that direction. The compass and turning-file business are permitted P-01 staging.

research.claim: The Soviet-pattern manpack radio, whip antenna, handset placement, and use of red light are presented as period equipment/detail.
research.note: The ledger documents radio traffic and silence, but does not source this specific radio model/configuration or red-light procedure.

flags.detail: The beat fixes the company's first steps into the marsh at night, but the ledger does not establish the exact time for this moment.
The specific Soviet-pattern manpack radio configuration, whip antenna, handset placement, and red-light decoding procedure are not sourced in the ledger.

direction.coverage: Begin tight profile insert on Mahmoud and note, then hold a restrained medium close-up as he raises his eyes into darkness.
direction.blocking: Mahmoud stays crouched at the marsh edge, note low in one hand and red-filtered torch angled beneath it, gaze lifting without turning.
direction.performance_note: Let the warning emerge as a breath-thin whisper, lips barely parting as alarm registers behind taped wire-rims.
direction.pacing: Slow, suspended hold with no cut after the whispered warning.
direction.tone_ref: Grounded wartime dread—red practical glow swallowed by marsh-black shadow.

wardrobe.additions: short military haircut, backpack field radio with a whip antenna (PRP-0007); wire-rimmed glasses taped at the hinge
visible_details: Taped wire-rimmed glasses, with the small red-filtered torch glow glinting along the taped hinge and lower rim.
Bare-headed short black military haircut; no helmet or headgear.
Sand-khaki cotton jacket at the profile neckline and shoulder, with plain khaki collar and no rank tabs, chest eagle, or modern insignia.
Aged khaki canvas chest-rig strap and plain metal buckle may edge into the lower shadowed frame; no modern tactical vest.
PRP-0007 manpack radio remains strapped high on his back, only a dark shoulder-side edge or antenna base if it enters the tight profile composition.
No weapon, watch, or modern equipment visible.
wardrobe.notes: Continuity from 2.4-01: same taped glasses, bare head, rolled-sleeve commando uniform and high-carried radio. WEAR_MUD reads chiefly as damp darkened jacket fabric, subtle brine sheen, and small mud flecks at the jaw/lower cheek; soaked trousers and boots remain out of this close frame.

makeup.skin_state: Light wheat skin is damp with exertion, with freckles faintly visible across the nose and upper cheek in the low red practical glow; restrained brine sheen and fine dark mud flecks sit along the jaw, lower cheek, and temple. No blood or visible wound.
makeup.hair_state: Bare-headed short black military haircut, damp and flattened at the temples; sparse brows and curled mustache are wet but intact, with a trace of brine catching the red light.
makeup.notes: Keep most facial detail swallowed by shadow: only the readable profile plane, slightly parted lips, taped wire-rimmed glasses, mustache edge, and one alarmed eye catch the dim red flashlight bounced from the paper. Preserve the actor's oval face, prominent cheekbones, freckles, light stubble, and curled mustache.

hand_items: small red-filtered flashlight angled beneath an unmarked decoding scrap
small weather-softened paper scrap with no legible writing
dressing: thin white salt crust over black mud at the crouched marsh edge
shallow brine sheet and small still reflective puddles below mid-shin level
sparse wet salt ridges and tiny mud clods near his knees
featureless black-blue marsh horizon swallowed by darkness
set.set_state: The flat Tina Plain marsh is cold, wet, and undisturbed, with firm salt-crusted mud broken by shallow brine pockets and no visible structures, vehicles, debris, or other troops.
set.notes: PRP-0007 remains strapped high on Mahmoud's back above the brine line as the active radio set; only its shoulder silhouette, strap, and a restrained antenna edge may enter the close frame. Keep the red practical confined to the paper, fingers, lower cheek, and taped glasses rim; moonlight supplies only a faint cool edge.

camera.light: Use the dim red-filtered flashlight as the sole facial key, angled up from beneath the decoded paper to model Mahmoud’s near-profile mouth, lower cheek, taped glasses and fingertips; retain only a near-black blue moon/starlight edge on his rear shoulder and marsh silhouette, with no fill.
camera.exposure_note: Expose for the small red practical without clipping the paper or glasses glint; hold the surrounding marsh 2–3 stops under so the profile and lip-sync mouth remain barely but clearly readable in deep blue-black shadow.
camera.framing_note: Generate 16:9 with Mahmoud’s profile eye, taped glasses, whispering mouth, both hands, red-lit paper and torch contained in the central middle 75% height for the 2.39:1 crop; keep the 85mm background fully soft and featureless.

action.choreography: Mahmoud holds a low, stable crouch at the marsh edge, keeping the manpack radio high on his back and the decoded scrap close to his chest. He slowly raises only his eyes toward the darkness without turning his profile, then releases the warning as a breath-thin whisper.
action.movement: Restrained crouched stillness; hands remain controlled around the note and red-filtered flashlight.
beats: Low crouch settles on firm salt-crusted mud.
One hand holds the decoded scrap low.
Red-filtered flashlight stays angled up beneath the paper.
His gaze lifts without turning his head.
Lips part for a quiet warning; body remains motionless.
action.safety_note: Use a stable crouch on the firmer marsh edge; avoid slipping or dropping the radio into the shallow brine.

It retains the key dramatic action without adding unsupported historical claims.

It references the available character and location library IDs. The radio, flashlight, and decoded note are appropriately treated as props/story-beat items; no missing ID is required under the stated rule.
Coverage, blocking, performance direction, pacing, and tone reference are all explicitly present.
The direction preserves Mahmoud’s required profile, crouched marsh-edge position, decoded note, red-filtered flashlight, taped wire-rimmed glasses, lifted gaze, and whispered warning.
The slow held pacing and restrained performance support the tense, hushed, alarmed intent without introducing melodrama or stylistic excess.
The visual language of a red practical source consumed by deep marsh shadow is consistent with a grounded historical war drama at night.

The mud/brine wear treatment and facial-level mud flecks are consistent with the prior shot while appropriately limiting lower-body detail outside the close framing.

The shadow treatment supports the locked requirement that his face not be clearly visible while retaining a readable profile eye, mouth, glasses, and lip-sync performance. No graphic injury is introduced.

The red flashlight is correctly treated as the sole meaningful facial illumination, with only a minimal cool rear edge consistent with the locked night setting.
The action is concrete and restrained: Mahmoud remains crouched, holds the note and filtered light under control, lifts his gaze without turning, and whispers the warning.
The choreography keeps the radio high and dry, introduces no unsupported combat event, and matches the tense, hushed scene intent.
